decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom represents a large development investment with an announced release in Q1/2019, so the firm is publicly committed to it and has had no time to see results.
The small volume chamber fits the core dosimetry portfolio and has its own page, and early-stage results can still be attributed to the launch ramp-up, so management will persist.
This second small volume chamber overlaps somewhat with B, which raises the chance of consolidation, but sunk development and calibration investment favor keeping it for now.
The standard clinical chamber line has several models and is central to the firm's dosimetry identity, so dropping it would write off substantial investment.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the firm's scanning and water phantom systems, which supports its strategic justification and makes it likely to be retained.
The thimble chamber is a core catalog item with low ongoing cost, and after only one year there is no evidence of failure that would force the firm to admit a mistake.
